title: Injective module H1 vanishing
statement: For a scheme Y and commutative ring Λ, an injective sheaf J of Λ-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] has subsingleton degree-one cohomology of its underlying abelian sheaf, where H¹ is Ext out of the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Let F be the underlying abelian sheaf of J. For every covering family of every object U, its first Cech cohomology vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-etale-module-cech-h1]. Only degree one is needed.

Fix any short exact sequence 0 → F → E → Q → 0 of abelian sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ses-cech-h1-surjective] at the terminal etale object T = (Y → Y), taking Cov to be all coverings. Every chosen family is a covering by definition; each covering refines itself, with the same indices and identity refinement maps. The Cech hypothesis is Step 1. Thus every section of Q at T lifts to E.

Use the proved library theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.subsingleton_H_one_of_surjective (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafCohomology.Basic). Its hypothesis is exactly Step 2, and T is terminal by MorphismProperty.Over.mkIdTerminal. The theorem embeds F into an injective abelian sheaf, represents every Ext¹ class by the connecting homomorphism of its cokernel sequence, and kills that class because the cokernel section lifts. This gives Subsingleton (Sheaf.H F 1).

proof_origin.place: Lemma 03FD, degree-one case of its second paragraph, via 03FC and 03F8; Ext vanishing from the proved library section-lifting theorem
